rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
Rough-cut drafts for articles.
Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named technique/practitioner paraphrased; creator-name and author-we grep also clean; onboarding email is a listed carve-out surface for "the trainer".

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
Over-hedge detector.
Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No user-supplied verbal frame requiring verbatim capture.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner attribution in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No punchy slogan/reframe present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
Watch out for planting jargon too early.
Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No forcing function was trimmed out of body prose here; the maintainer note describes an earlier structural collapse to a link, not a mid-sentence trim leaving dangling pronouns.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an onboarding email, not an exercise; no recap-block convention applies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only header is the H1 title, no metaphor/mechanism mismatch.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No enumerated list in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No superlative/slogan claim present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `<!-- backing -->` claim ledger or cited source claim in this file's body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This rule governs sweep-authoring discipline across multiple files, not a single body-prose surface being judged in isolation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Module 1" is spelled out in full form (correct for a pre-M1/prework-adjacent surface); "Claude Code" is a product name, not a curriculum-coined term needing a primer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule is scoped to the Agents 101 (business-leader) audience default; this file is an AE101 (software-engineer) onboarding email and its vocabulary (repo, Module 1, Claude Code) is already-familiar engineer language, governed instead by rule 2's earn-on-first-use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither term used in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Anything trips you up, reply to this email and I'll sort it with you" (line 13) is a single, minimal rescue line, not a troubleshooting FAQ branch; it fits the rule's boundary exception for a needed recovery staying in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt blocks in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module — never repeat same Debrief.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No retro/Debrief content in an onboarding email.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Single short logistics email, no module-specific mood or voice being borrowed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No instruction lines directing student action on Claude's output at all.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No self-study simulation content.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No student moves specified in this file (no prompts, no exercise forcing function).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No CLAUDE.md reference in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No em-dashes in body; sentences are short and simple.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No subsection headers in body beyond the H1 title.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No session/task/run vocabulary used in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "the morning of Module 1" (line 13) names a real calendar point (Day 1 start), not a banned relative time-of-day anchor (tomorrow/this morning/overnight/etc.), and does not assume any particular inter-module gap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompts or decision beats in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No file-saving instruction in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body is already lean (maintainer note records it was collapsed from a four-section restatement to a link); each remaining sentence carries logistics the reader needs to act.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No chat-print moment in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Looking forward to it." is a personal email sign-off (subject = the trainer), not a forward-looking callout gesturing at what the student will find across the training.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No per-module operational settings (thinking-effort, model, mode tag) discussed in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Echo the training's theory spine before inventing a synonym.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Pure logistics email; no teaching vocabulary choice at stake.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No description of sending a message to the agent ("typing", "type in", etc. all absent).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body states outcomes ("Everything to do before then is here") and defers all setup mechanics to the prework link and maintainer-recorded collapse, exactly the pattern this rule asks for.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 7: "The training is hands-on from minute one." — subject is "the training", describing its own shape rather than the student's repo/task/decision. Deletion test: cutting it leaves "We start Module 1 of Agentic Engineering 101 on [Day 1 date and time]. You'll be writing real code on your real repo, with Claude Code running on your laptop, the whole way through." which joins cleanly and already carries the same information concretely.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; the following sentence already shows hands-on-from-minute-one concretely.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: CTO-repeatable test.
